families.product_name: Kosmos (Auto EF, AI FAST, AI Trio)
families.summary: Kosmos is a handheld/ultraportable diagnostic ultrasound system (phased-array Torso/Torso-One and linear Lexsa probes) first cleared in March 2020 with integrated ECG and digital auscultation. The 2024 clearance K233826 added product code QIH and an Indications for Use that names the AI-assisted automated ejection fraction software (Auto EF) and Auto Anatomical Structure Labeling and View Identification (AI FAST); K242321 (2025) covers the Kosmos-on-Android configuration with OB/GYN, TDI and color power Doppler. No FDA-summary performance data are public for the AI features because K233826 and K242321 were filed with 510(k) Statements rather than Summaries.
families.intended_use_quote: Kosmos is intended to be used by qualified and trained healthcare professionals in the clinical assessment for the following clinical applications by acquiring, processing, displaying, measuring, and storing ultrasound images, or synchronized ultrasound images, electrocardiogram (ECG) rhythms, and digital auscultation (DA) sounds and waveforms.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Kosmos is intended to be used by qualified and trained healthcare professionals in the clinical assessment for the following clinical applications by acquiring, processing, displaying, measuring, and storing ultrasound images, or synchronized ultrasound images, electrocardiogram (ECG) rhythms, and digital auscultation (DA) sounds and waveforms. With respect to its ultrasound imaging capability, Kosmos is a general-purpose diagnostic ultrasound system used in the following clinical applications and modes of operation: Clinical Applications: Cardiac, Thoracic/Lung, Abdominal, Vascular/Peripheral Vascular, Musculoskeletal, and interventional guidance (includes free hand needle / catheter placement fluid drainage, and nerve block) Modes of Operation: B-mode, M-mode, Color Doppler, Pulsed Wave (PW) Doppler, Continuous Wave (CW) Doppler, Combined Modes of B+M, and B+CD, B+PW, B+CW, and Harmonic Imaging. Kosmos is intended to be used in clinical care and medical education settings on adult and pediatric patient populations. Kosmos includes the AI-assisted automated ejection fraction software, known as Auto EF, which is used to process previously acquired transthoracic cardiac ultrasound images, to store images, and to manipulate and make measurements on images using the Kosmos. Auto EF provides automated estimation of left ventricular ejection fraction. This measurement can be used to assist the clinician in a cardiac evaluation. Auto EF is indicated for use on adult patients only in healthcare facilities. The Kosmos includes the Auto Anatomical Structure Labeling and View Identification, also referred to as AI FAST, software, which is intended for use only by qualified and trained medical professionals for automatic real-time detection and labeling of anatomical structures during image acquisition during cardiac, thoracic/lung, or abdominal ultrasound imaging. This feature is only indicated for use on adult patients in healthcare facilities. The device is non-invasive, reusable, and intended to be used on one patient at a time.
embedded_ai_features: Auto EF: AI-assisted automated left ventricular ejection fraction from previously acquired transthoracic clips (adults; named in K233826 IFU)
AI FAST: automatic real-time detection and labeling of anatomical structures and view identification during cardiac, lung, or abdominal imaging (adults; named in K233826 IFU)

AI Trio: real-time guidance, image grading and anatomical labeling for cardiac views (described in K212100 as 'not yet cleared', marketed under the COVID-19 imaging enforcement policy; company site lists Trio under Kosmos EDU; clearance status not confirmed in any IFU read)
Auto Doppler (PW/TDI sample-gate placement) and Auto Preset (company-described features; not named in IFU)
Kosmos Bladder AI volume (company-described; clearance not covered by the K-numbers in this batch)

clearances.changes_summary: Original Kosmos clearance: tablet + phased-array probe with integrated 3-lead single-channel ECG and digital auscultation; B-mode, M-mode, color Doppler, harmonic imaging; cardiac, lung, abdominal, peripheral vascular, needle guidance. No AI features. 'An assessment of clinical performance data for KOSMOS was not required to support a determination of substantial equivalence.' (p. 9)
notable_flags: additional product codes IYO, ITX, DQD, DPS

clearances.changes_summary: Added Kosmos Lexsa linear-array probe, Torso-One and Torso-One USB ultrasound-only probes, Kosmos on Android (off-the-shelf tablet) configuration, PW and CW Doppler, musculoskeletal/vascular/nerve-block applications. Summary states: 'Kosmos is an FDA-cleared medical device; however, the new AI-assisted EF Workflow and Trio tool are not yet cleared by the FDA. Instead, EchoNous is following the Enforcement Policy for Imaging Systems During the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Public Health Emergency' (p. 6). Clinical performance data not required (p. 14).
notable_flags: AI EF/Trio marketed under COVID-19 enforcement policy, not cleared in this K

clearances.changes_summary: 510(k) Statement (no public summary). Product codes expanded to IYN, IYO, ITX, DQD, DPS, QIH. The Indications for Use adds the AI-assisted automated ejection fraction software (Auto EF) for previously acquired transthoracic images in adults and the Auto Anatomical Structure Labeling and View Identification software (AI FAST) for real-time labeling during cardiac, lung or abdominal imaging in adults. Predicates and performance data are not public.
notable_flags: AI features first named in IFU

clearances.changes_summary: 510(k) Statement (no public summary). IFU covers 'Clinical Applications and Modes of Operation for Kosmos on Android': Torso-One for Cardiac, Thoracic/Lung, Abdominal and Obstetrics/Gynecology; Lexsa for Lung, Vascular, MSK, Nerve and needle guidance; adds Color Power Doppler and TDI. Product codes IYN, IYO, ITX only; the ECG/auscultation and Auto EF / AI FAST language of K233826 is not present in this IFU.
notable_flags: TDI and color power Doppler added

performance_claims.endpoint: Kosmos autoEF vs cardiac MRI LVEF
performance_claims.value: r = 0.99; bias 1.1%; median LVEF 57% (CMR) vs 55% (AI-Echo), p = 0.51
performance_claims.comparator: cardiac magnetic resonance LVEF
performance_claims.dataset_description: 49 adult patients undergoing clinically indicated CMR, single Italian center, prospective
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Source: peer-reviewed abstract, Bisignani 2025 (doi 10.3390/jcm14134708); not from an FDA submission. Software version relative to K233826 is not stated in the paper.
performance_claims.quote: Median LVEF was 57% (CMR) vs. 55% (AI-Echo), with no significant difference (p = 0.51). Strong correlation (r = 0.99) and minimal bias (1.1%) were observed.

performance_claims.endpoint: Kosmos autoEF (TRIO AI + KOSMOS EF) vs standard echo biplane Simpson's LVEF, by operator
performance_claims.value: cardiologist r = 0.90; junior oncologist r = 0.82; nurse r = 0.84; senior oncologist r = 0.79
performance_claims.comparator: biplane Simpson's LVEF on standard echocardiography by cardiologist
performance_claims.dataset_description: 115 patients referred for echocardiographic LVEF estimation (chemotherapy/oncology setting); each scanned by cardiologist, senior oncologist, oncology resident and nurse with Kosmos HUD
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Source: peer-reviewed abstract, Papadopoulou 2024 (doi 10.1093/ehjdh/ztae017); not from an FDA submission. Software version relative to K233826 is not stated in the paper. Bland-Altman showed small underestimation by autoEF vs SE-EF
performance_claims.quote: The correlation between autoEF and SE-ejection fraction (EF) was excellent for the cardiologist (r = 0.90), the junior oncologist (r = 0.82), and the nurse (r = 0.84), and good for the senior oncologist (r = 0.79).

performance_claims.endpoint: Detection of LVEF < 50% with Kosmos autoEF, by operator
performance_claims.value: cardiologist 95%/94%; senior oncologist 86%/93%; junior oncologist 95%/91%; nurse 94%/87%
performance_claims.comparator: biplane Simpson's LVEF on standard echocardiography
performance_claims.dataset_description: same cohort as above
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Source: peer-reviewed abstract, Papadopoulou 2024 (doi 10.1093/ehjdh/ztae017); not from an FDA submission. Software version relative to K233826 is not stated in the paper.
performance_claims.quote: Detection of impaired LVEF < 50% was feasible with a sensitivity of 95% and specificity of 94% for the cardiologist; sensitivity of 86% and specificity of 93% for the senior oncologist; sensitivity of 95% and specificity of 91% for the junior oncologist; and sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 87% for the nurse.

performance_claims.endpoint: AI-enhanced novice pathway (Kosmos AI-guided acquisition by novices + Us2.ai automated reporting) for detecting LVEF < 50%
performance_claims.value: AUC 0.880 (95% CI 0.802-0.958); sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 91.4%, PPV 78.5%, NPV 94.1%; median absolute LVEF deviation 6.03%
performance_claims.comparator: standard echo by trained sonographers interpreted by cardiologists
performance_claims.dataset_description: 100 symptomatic patients with suspected HF (mean age 61 +/- 15, 56% men); novices with 2 weeks' training; interpretable in 96 patients
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Source: peer-reviewed abstract, Huang 2024 (doi 10.1038/s41598-024-62467-4); not from an FDA submission. Software version relative to K233826 is not stated in the paper. LVEF reported by Us2.ai software, not Kosmos Auto EF; Kosmos supplied AI acquisition guidance
performance_claims.quote: The area under the curve (AUC) of the AI novice pathway was 0.880 (95% CI 0.802, 0.958). The sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive and negative predictive values of the AI-enhanced novice pathway in detecting LVEF < 50% were 84.6%, 91.4%, 78.5% and 94.1% respectively.

performance_claims.endpoint: Kosmos automatic LVEF (AI-POCUS) vs biplane disk-method LVEF on high-end echo, two Japanese hospitals
performance_claims.value: ICC 0.81; mean bias -1.5% (limits of agreement +/- 15.0%); LVEF < 50% sensitivity 85% (95% CI 76-91%), specificity 81% (71-89%)
performance_claims.comparator: standard biplane disk method on high-end ultrasound machines
performance_claims.dataset_description: 200 patients prospectively scanned at two Japanese hospitals; 18 excluded for infeasible AI images; 182 analysed (63 +/- 15 years, 21% female). Device identified in full text as KOSMOS (EchoNous Inc.) with company-developed automatic LVEF program; study partially funded by EchoNous.
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Source: peer-reviewed abstract, Kagiyama 2024 (doi 10.1038/s41598-024-65557-5); not from an FDA submission. LV volumes underestimated for larger LVs (EDV bias 42.1 mL); a newer software version showed ICC > 0.85 for volumes. Software version relative to K233826 not stated.
performance_claims.quote: The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) between the LVEF by AI-POCUS and the standard methods was good (0.81, p < 0.001) without clinically meaningful systematic bias (mean bias -1.5%, p = 0.008, limits of agreement ± 15.0%). Reduced LVEF < 50% was detected with a sensitivity of 85% (95% confidence interval 76%-91%) and specificity of 81% (71%-89%).

training_data.description: No training-set size or composition is stated in K193518 or K212100; K233826 and K242321 are 510(k) Statements with no public summary. No peer-reviewed algorithm-development paper for Auto EF or AI FAST was found.

validation_data.description: FDA test-set description not public (Statements). Company pivotal registrations: NCT06027164 'Kosmos Trio and Ejection Fraction Pivotal Study' (n=153 actual, nurses vs sonographers, LVEF vs cardiologist panel; collaborators UCSF, Revival Research Institute, Centaur Labs) and NCT06468787 'Kosmos Anatomical Object Labeling and View Identification Pivotal Study' (n=32, multi-site, false discovery rate endpoints). Linkage of these studies to K233826 is inferred from timing, not confirmed by FDA documents.

prior_validations.description: Company 'Kosmos AI EF clinical validation' landing page: prospective study of 78 patients at Mercy Med Clinic (Columbus, GA), four echocardiographers, reference = average of two independent echo core labs (Massachusetts General Hospital and UCSF); results gated behind a download form and not read. (echonous.com returned HTTP 403 at fact-check on 2026-09-05; figures could not be re-confirmed.)

Company clinical-benchmarking page: AI-based EF in n=100 (mean age 57+/-15, BMI 28+/-4, 61% male) vs cart-based Simpson's biplane: correlation 0.87 (p<0.0001), bias 1.42%, RMSD 7.51%; CW Doppler velocities in n=50 vs high-end cart: correlation 0.98, bias 0.15 m/s, RMSD 0.26 m/s. Unpublished company data. (echonous.com returned HTTP 403 at fact-check on 2026-09-05; figures could not be re-confirmed.)

Hardware (non-AI) validation of Kosmos CW Doppler for aortic stenosis: 101 patients, mean gradient ICC 0.87, r = 0.89, kappa 0.81 for severe AS (Zubiaur 2024); TAVI prosthesis assessment in 64 patients, mean gradient ICC 0.76, Vmax ICC 0.83 (Margarida de Castro 2026).

open_questions: K233826 and K242321 were filed as 510(k) Statements: predicate devices, test-set size, sites, comparator and all performance metrics for Auto EF and AI FAST are not public.
Whether NCT06027164 (n=153) and NCT06468787 (n=32) are the pivotal datasets behind K233826 is inferred from sponsor and timing only; not confirmed by FDA documents.
Training-set size and composition for Auto EF / AI FAST / Trio are undisclosed in every source read.
Company AI EF validation (n=78, MGH and UCSF core labs) results are behind a download gate and were not read; metrics unknown.

AI Trio guidance/grading clearance status is unclear: K212100 says 'not yet cleared' (COVID-19 enforcement policy); the K233826 IFU names Auto EF and AI FAST but not Trio guidance; company lists Trio under Kosmos EDU. NCT07771270 (2026) is still evaluating Trio guidance.
K242321 IFU (Kosmos on Android) omits the Auto EF and AI FAST language and the ECG/DA text; whether the Android configuration carries the AI features under K233826 is not stated.
Kosmos PLAX EF (Teichholz) is under pivotal study in 2026 (NCT07771231) and is not covered by any K-number in this batch.

No peer-reviewed paper reports Kosmos Auto EF performance against the FDA reference standard; published validations are single-center (n=49 vs CMR; n=115 vs biplane Simpson's) or two-center (n=182 vs biplane disk method, Kagiyama 2024, with 9% of patients excluded for infeasible AI images).

families.product_name: Exo AI Platform (AIP001 / AIP002) and Strain AI (SAI001)
deployment: on-device (Exo Iris handheld; company states the AI runs on the device without internet connectivity)
software module / API integrated into a legally marketed ultrasound system
families.summary: Exo's AI Platform is a DICOM-input software-as-a-medical-device (product code QIH) first cleared in November 2023 with LVEF AI (AP4, AP2, biplane and PLAX views) and Lung AI (A-line presence, B-line count). AI Platform 2.0 (August 2024) added interventricular septum and posterior wall thickness, IVC minimum/maximum diameter, real-time frame and clip Quality AI, delivery of the algorithms as an accessory API for integration into ultrasound systems, and a Predetermined Change Control Plan. Strain AI (November 2024) adds global longitudinal strain from the apical 4-chamber view with the Us2.v2 output as reference standard, and AI Platform 2.2 (Special 510(k), February 2026) extends Quality AI to abdominal upper-quadrant and pelvic views. The company markets these on the Exo Iris handheld as SweepAI running on-device.
families.intended_use_quote: Exo AI Platform is a software as a medical device (SaMD) that helps qualified users with image-based assessment of ultrasound examinations in adult patients. It is designed to simplify workflow by helping trained healthcare providers evaluate, quantify, and generate reports for ultrasound images.
families.indications_for_use_quote: AI Platform 2.2 is intended for noninvasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease. In addition, it can provide Quality Score feedback to assist healthcare professionals, trained and qualified to conduct echocardiography, abdominal, and lung ultrasound scans in the current standard of care while acquiring ultrasound images. The device is intended to be used on images of adult patients.
embedded_ai_features: LVEF AI: AI-assisted ejection fraction from AP4, AP2, biplane and PLAX views (K232501)
Lung AI: presence/absence of A-lines and B-line count, with per-frame and per-clip quality score (K232501; quality in K240953)
Cardiac AI wall thickness: IVSd and PWd from PLAX (K240953)
IVC AI: minimum diameter on inspiration and maximum diameter on expiration (K240953)
Quality AI: real-time per-frame and per-clip quality score for A4C, PLAX, lung (K240953) and abdominal upper-quadrant and pelvic views (K260217); retrospective recording of diagnostic-quality clip
Strain AI: global longitudinal strain from A4C clips, user can accept or reject (K242359)
Stroke volume (company-described output derived from LVEF module; not separately named in FDA summaries)

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance of AI Platform (AIP001): DICOM-input SaMD with LVEF AI (AP4, AP2, biplane, PLAX) and Lung AI (A-lines, B-lines). Predicate LVivo Software Application (DiA, K210053); reference Philips Lumify (K223771). Deep CNNs for segmentation/landmark detection; manual editing allowed.

AI Platform 2.0 (AIP002): adds myocardial wall thickness (IVSd, PWd from PLAX), IVC Dmin/Dmax, real-time per-frame and per-clip Quality AI for A4C, PLAX and lung with retrospective capture of diagnostic-quality clips, and packaging of the algorithms/API as accessory modules for integration into legally marketed ultrasound systems. 'The A-Line, B-line and LVEF algorithms did not change during the development of the AI Platform 2.0 product and remain as per the cleared algorithms in K232501.' (p. 12). PCCP covers (A) architecture/pre-post-processing modifications and (B) new training data, with non-inferiority testing and manual (not automatic) retraining.

Strain AI (SAI001): new SaMD module computing global longitudinal strain from A4C clips, delivered as a module without built-in viewer for integration into a third-party ultrasound device; post-processing; user may accept or reject. Predicate LVivo (K210053); reference Us2.v2 (K233676), which also served as ground truth.
notable_flags: ground truth from reference device Us2.v2

clearances.changes_summary: Special 510(k) for AI Platform 2.2 (AIP002): extends Quality AI to abdominal upper-quadrant and pelvic views; intended use, architecture, workflow unchanged. The K240953 PCCP is retained but 'the subject modifications described in this submission are outside the scope of the PCCP' (p. 7). Lung and cardiac functionalities unchanged from K240953.

training_data.description: FDA summaries give no training-set size; they state only that test data were 'entirely separated from the training/validation datasets' and drawn from data sources different from the training sources (K232501 p. 7; K242359 p. 7 adds 'acquired from independent clinical sites'). Company press release (April 23, 2024) states the AI was trained on 'over 100,000 images from point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) exams performed by users in real-world settings, including emergency rooms and critical care units.' The K240953 PCCP permits augmenting training data with manual retraining.

validation_data.description: K232501: LVEF tested on 151 subjects and lung on 125 subjects from 'multiple clinical sites in metropolitan cities with diverse racial patient populations', gender, age 20-96, BMI 15.3-52.8, cart-based and portable scanners; ground truth = mean of three experts. K240953: wall thickness and IVC on 100 subjects each; Quality AI on 184 patients/226 clips retrospective plus 396 prospective scans by 26 users. K242359: GLS subject count not legible in summary; ground truth = Us2.v2. K260217: abdominal Quality AI on 184 patients/200 clips plus 186 prospective scans by 12 users.

prior_validations.description: Company AI page reproduces the Vega 2024 Diagnostics LVEF results (RMSE 7.58% A2C, 7.45% A4C, 7.29% PLAX; low-EF accuracy 83/80/91%) as its published validation; states SweepAI runs 'without internet or cloud reliance' while Thyroid AI is cloud-based.

Press release April 23, 2024: cardiac (LVEF, stroke volume; PLAX and A4C) and lung (B-lines) AI launched on Exo Iris; 'five different applications—cardiac, lung, bladder, hip and thyroid' cleared; trained on 'over 100,000 images' from real-world POCUS exams.
Press release December 4, 2024: IVC collapsibility and posterior/septal wall thickness added to Exo Iris (SweepAI); 'Exo's AI runs on-edge—no Wi-Fi required'; no performance data.
Press release April 2, 2025: 510(k)-cleared GLS on Exo Iris described by the company as its 10th FDA-cleared AI application; no performance data.

open_questions: K242359 (Strain AI): the number of test subjects is missing from the summary text ('The Strain function was evaluated with subjects'); n unknown. RMSD 2.76 is reported without units.

Training-set sizes are absent from all four FDA summaries; the 'over 100,000 images' figure is a company press-release claim and its split across LVEF, lung, wall-thickness, IVC, GLS and quality models is unknown.
Number of test sites is never stated ('multiple clinical sites in metropolitan cities'); ultrasound vendors are not named.
K240953 and K260217 both cite retrospective Quality AI cohorts of '184 patients'; whether these are the same patients is not stated.
Whether the 441-patient Vega 2024 dataset overlaps the 151-subject FDA LVEF test set is unknown.
GLS ground truth is the Us2.v2 algorithm output rather than expert speckle-tracking; no expert-reference GLS validation was found.
Subgroup performance (gender, BMI, image quality, vendor) is asserted as 'consistent' but no subgroup numbers are given in any summary.

Company counts of 9-10 cleared AI applications include bladder, hip, thyroid and pleural effusion/consolidation clearances that are not among the K-numbers in this batch; their K-numbers were not researched here.
No registered clinical trial specific to the Exo AI Platform or Strain AI was identified on clinicaltrials.gov (searches for Exo Iris / Exo Imaging returned only hip-dysplasia and unrelated studies).

notes: Fact-checked 2026-09-05. All FDA quotes, values, page numbers, predicates, decision dates and product codes were re-checked against the eight FDA text files and openFDA; no numeric disagreements were found. K233826 page 3 (image-only) was rendered from the PDF and the IFU quote confirmed visually. K242359 does not state the GLS test-set size in either the text extraction or pypdf (the number is absent from the PDF text layer). All 17 papers were resolved via Crossref and PubMed efetch; abstract quotes match. Performance claims taken from peer-reviewed papers are now unlinked from K-numbers (k_number null) because the FDA records do not contain them and the papers do not state which cleared software version was tested. EchoNous company pages returned HTTP 403 at fact-check, so company-only Kosmos figures are marked unverified. Exo press-release quotes ('over 100,000 images', 'five different applications', '10th FDA-cleared AI application') were confirmed on exo.inc. Added from extra PubMed searches: Kagiyama 2024 (two-center Kosmos AI-LVEF validation), Tromp 2024 CUMIN, Papadopoulou 2026, Gomez-Alvarez 2024; no new Exo product papers were found beyond those already listed.
